clue.text: Nothing perceptible initially, standing in shadow

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

indicators.note: initially says only the opening letter of the word perceptible is wanted

parts.note: one's standing is one's position or rank

explanation.surface: Something barely visible at first, lurking in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shadow' is the British term for the opposition party's team mirroring government ministers, as in 'shadow cabinet'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British politics the party out of power forms a shadow cabinet, so the shadow side is the party facing the government.

clue.text: Performing team not anticipating referee's whistle?

parts.note: an actor performing is on stage, on
a team is a side in sport

explanation.surface: A team playing without jumping ahead of the referee blowing the whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: In football a player who runs beyond the defenders too early is offside and the referee whistles; staying level means not getting ahead of that whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer in a legal position has not strayed ahead of play, so gives the referee no reason to blow for offside.

clue.text: Poster designed quickly

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of poster are laid out afresh in a new pattern

explanation.surface: A poster was knocked up in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking meaning fast, and also an exclamation of sudden speed.

clue.text: Going around island, day works fine

indicators.note: going around says the day and works pieces surround the island abbreviation

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A day trip round an island where the factory runs smoothly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fine in the sense of acceptable or adequate is satisfactory, as in 'that's fine by me'.

clue.text: Catch not entirely lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the letters are read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: not entirely means only in part

explanation.surface: A catch that wasn't completely raised off the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A catch is a snare or trick designed to ensnare someone, which is what a trap does.

clue.text: Where television aerial is usually free

definitions.meaning: an aerial is normally fixed up on the roof of a home
free of charge, given at the expense of the establishment

explanation.surface: A note that the aerial on top of the building comes at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks given free by the landlord are offered at the establishment's expense; an aerial sits up on a building's roof.

clue.text: Meat plans rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests turned back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: plans of a building or area are maps

explanation.surface: Proposals for meat dishes are turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: Spam is a brand of tinned luncheon meat.

clue.text: Trace page, piece of newspaper?

parts.note: a piece in a newspaper is an article

explanation.surface: Hunting down a page or item from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a tiny amount, a speck or minute bit of something.

clue.text: Mat originally straightened, dragged through the mud

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word Mat

parts.note: straightened out means lined up, aligned

explanation.surface: A doormat was straightened out after being dragged through the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: To drag someone's name through the mud is to slander or speak ill of them unjustly.

clue.text: A step wasn't awkward in elasticated trousers

indicators.note: awkward implies the letters of a step wasn't are clumsily jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone moving smoothly despite wearing stretchy trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in wasn't is ignored; its letters join the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose tracksuit bottoms with elastic waists, worn for exercise, are a kind of trouser.

clue.text: Test returns in regular order

indicators.note: returns says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words regular order

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A test that comes back in the usual sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' unmarked; it is the signal that the letters are concealed inside regular order.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a test answered out loud.

clue.text: Great message about drone is broadcast

indicators.note: about says the message goes around the other letters

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, a message sent by wire

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of drone is are spread about

explanation.surface: A grand message about a drone goes out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great' reads as praise for the message but is the definition, meaning large in amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of large in amount or size, as a great deal is a sizeable one.

clue.text: Steed struggling with back in fact can't stand

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of steed are thrown about
back in points to the final letter of the word fact

explanation.surface: A struggling horse with a bad back is in fact unable to stand up.
explanation.definitionFit: If you can't stand something you loathe it, an idiom for strong dislike.

clue.text: Turning out to be appropriate

definitions.meaning: growing into or developing into something
suitable or flattering, as clothes that suit you

explanation.surface: Something proving to be suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense means coming to be, as a child grows into an adult; the other means fitting, as a hat flatters.

clue.text: Due to leave centre, release planned

indicators.note: to leave centre says the middle letter of due is dropped

parts.note: to release is to free, liberate

explanation.surface: A prisoner, scheduled to leave the centre, has a planned release.
explanation.definitionFit: A deliberate act is intended or premeditated rather than accidental.

clue.text: Nice unmarried woman?

parts.note: Nice is the French city, so the single woman is French; the French title for a young unmarried woman is the one wanted

explanation.surface: A pleasant single lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' reads as the adjective pleasant, but capitalised it is the city on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: The French courtesy title for an unmarried woman, equivalent to Miss, used by someone in Nice.

clue.text: Wonderful hitting tennis ball hard

definitions.meaning: an informal British word for splendid or terrific
a smash in tennis is a hard overhead shot struck downwards

explanation.surface: Praise for a player who hits the ball with real power.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for excellent, and the action of playing a forceful overhead tennis shot.

clue.text: Reject change, unhappy

parts.note: to turn is to change, as milk turns sour
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: Someone turning down a change and feeling glum about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To decline an offer or refuse an application is a phrasal verb for rejecting it.

clue.text: One's inclined to use admin in building

indicators.note: building suggests construction, so the letters of to use admin in are assembled anew

explanation.surface: Someone keen to make use of the admin office in a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of a peak is inclined ground, so 'one' that is inclined is a steep flank of a mountain.

clue.text: Unable to speak about fashionable time

indicators.note: about says the word for speechless wraps around the fashionable piece

parts.note: someone unable to speak is mute
in means trendy or fashionable

explanation.surface: A speechless person discussing a trendy period.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixtieth part of an hour is a unit of time.

clue.text: Very popular ruby stolen

parts.note: ruby is a deep red colour
hot goods are stolen ones

explanation.surface: A much-loved ruby has been nicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extremely in demand is said to be a red-hot favourite, the hottest property.

clue.text: Prepares tomatoes perhaps, and other items?

definitions.meaning: tomatoes are often dried in the sun, so this reads as a verb

explanation.surface: Getting tomatoes ready, along with other bits and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Miscellaneous small items not worth listing separately, and a split reading of drying in sunshine.

clue.text: Reportedly, gangs drift along

indicators.note: reportedly suggests the word is as heard spoken, not as written

parts.note: gangs of workers are crews

explanation.surface: Word has it that gangs are wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: To move at a steady easy pace, as a ship or car does at cruising speed.

clue.text: Testament maintained by perfect opponent

indicators.note: maintained by says the testament is held inside the word for perfect

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written with I standing for one
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A will is upheld by an ideal adversary.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is against something is anti it; used as a noun the word names an opposer.

clue.text: I rip off image

parts.note: a rip-off is a swindle, a con

explanation.surface: Someone confessing to tearing off a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious painting or a symbol on a screen is a representation, a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Constable would have had one tidying up trash in pub

indicators.note: tidying up implies putting the letters of trash in pub into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman would have had one clearing rubbish in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constable' looks like a police officer but is John Constable, the English landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter like John Constable needed a bristled tool to apply colour to canvas.

clue.text: Charming man, spy needing no introduction

indicators.note: needing no introduction says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A charming spy so famous he needs no introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: A courteous, well-mannered male is short for a gentleman.

clue.text: Polish were fine men, though not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the phrase were fine men, though is used, the letters concealed within

explanation.surface: Polish men were fine, though only up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the noun meaning elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish here means sophistication or elegance of manner, cultivated finesse.
